title: QBR playbook: Atlas Manufacturing — Exec & Ops narrative (draft)
content:
Purpose and context:
- This is a working draft of the QBR narrative and slide-by-slide speaker notes for Atlas Manufacturing (primary contacts: Marisol Vega, CTO; Dinesh Kumar, Head of Automation). Goal = align execs on value delivered, identify runway threats for renewal (Q3 2026), and surface 1–2 clear asks (budget + pilot expansion).

Meeting logistics (target):
- Audience: Marisol (CTO), Dinesh (Head Automation), Procurement lead, Plant Ops Director, our AE + CSM + Solutions Eng
- Duration: 45 minutes (20m exec narrative, 15m technical deep-dive, 10m next steps + Q&A)
- Desired outcomes: exec sign-off on renewal term + greenlight for pilot of Dedicated capacity for two plants; commitment to provide production prompt set for quality monitoring integration.

Top-level narrative (elevator pitch):
- We helped Atlas reduce manual exception investigation time by ~42% across two pilot sites using our hosted chat and reranking flows. Platform uptime 99.97% last quarter; average inference latency 230ms P95 for short prompts (supply-chain queries). Renewing with a 12-month committed capacity + the Dedicated pilot unlocks deterministic latency and ~28% unit-cost drop based on our batching/quantization recommendations.

Slide-by-slide breakdown + speaker notes:
1) Title / Welcome (1 slide)
- Note: quick agenda, set timing expectations.

2) Business outcomes snapshot (1 slide)
- KPIs to show: Exceptions handled (pilot): 1,420 -> 2,010 Q-over-Q (manual hours saved est. 540 hrs), average fulfillment lead time improvement +6.8%, incident MTTR down 34%.
- Talking point: tie saved hours to headcount redeploy opportunity in Plant 3.

3) Usage & reliability (1 slide)
- Tokens/day: ~2.2M; peak tokens/min: 18k; 99.97% uptime last 90d.
- Latency profile: median 120ms, P95 230ms (hosted), P95 for current on-prem model variant ~420ms.
- Cost highlight: current effective cost $0.0045 / 1k tokens after caching; Dedicated pilot projection $0.0032 / 1k tokens.
- Note to speaker: emphasize predictable cost math — attach appendix with cost model.

4) Quality and regression monitoring (1 slide)
- Eval summary: 8 curated prompt families used, aggregate pass rate 91% (definition: top-1 answer within acceptance rules). Recent regression spike flagged on prompt family 'SKU normalization' (falling from 94% to 86%).
- Root cause hypothesis: model version rollout + tokenizer edge cases on SKU format.
- Action: temporary fallback to previous model variant + need Atlas to share a canonical SKU list.

5) Reliability & incident summary (1 slide)
- Incidents: two minor outages (15m, 8m) due to network flapping during cloud region maintenance; automatic fallback worked, no customer-facing downtime.
- SRE actions taken: routing policy tweak, added cross-region warm capacity.

6) Technical deep-dive (2 slides)
- Architecture diagram (hosted + Dedicated pilot path) — speaker note: show how Dedicated integrates with Atlas VPC and HSM for keys.
- Performance levers: batching window tuning, KV cache policy, quantization recommendation (int8 dynamic) — expected latency/cost impacts with numbers.

7) Renewal health and risk register (1 slide)
- Health score 78/100 (green for reliability, amber for quality/regression, amber for procurement negotiation).
- Risks: open SKU normalization regression, contract lead time (procurement wants 60d for PO), data residency question for one EU plant.

8) Proposed commercial ask (1 slide)
- Renewal proposal: 12 months, committed tokens = 0.9B, 10% prepay discount + 6-month milestone for Dedicated pilot activation.
- Upsell opportunity: Dedicated capacity for 2 plants + Redwood Optimize package for continuous evals (+$X/month).
- Talking point: show ROI table (savings vs manual hours redeployed).

9) Operational asks + ownership (1 slide)
- Atlas deliverables: canonical SKU list, approval for network peering test window (2 weeks), procurement timeline (target: PO by 2026-05-15).
- Our deliverables: Dedicated pilot runbook, SLO/SLA draft, security checklist with HSM integration steps.

10) Next steps & close (1 slide)
- Immediate next steps: schedule technical kickoff (owners: Priya + Dinesh) week of 2026-03-22; secure commercial review meeting with procurement (AE + Sofia) by 2026-03-31.
- Ask: confirm decision maker present for renewal approval (Marisol or delegated).

Appendix (for handoff) — quick bullets to include in slide notes:
- Full cost model spreadsheet (link to Confluence page).
- Regression logs + example inputs for SKU normalization failure (attach in deck appendix).
- SRE runbook excerpt for cross-region failover.

Tailored talking points by stakeholder:
- CTO (Marisol): Focus on deterministic latency, security (HSM + VPC option), and roadmap alignment for predictive maintenance use-case. Ask: prioritize Dedicated pilot for Plant 1 and Plant 3 to validate 99ms median latency target.
- Head of Automation (Dinesh): Emphasize reduction in exception triage time and lowered false-positive reranking rate. Ask: provide production prompts and example failure cases.
- Procurement: Emphasize predictable unit economics and prepay discount structure; offer staggered billing tied to pilot milestones.
- Plant Ops: Highlight improvements to MTTR and headcount redeploy opportunities; propose 3-week engineering shadow for knowledge transfer.

Renewal negotiation levers (playbook snippets):
- If procurement pushes on price: offer a one-time 5% on committed tokens in exchange for 12-month commit with PO in 30 days.
- If security/residency is the blocker: propose temporary EU region Dedicated pool + expanded DPA addendum; schedule privacy brief with legal.
- If quality/regression concerns dominate: offer short-term rollback and prioritized engineering triage; include remediation SLA in the pilot terms.

Open questions / data we need from Atlas (to resolve before finalizing slides):
- Confirm procurement PO timeline and approval chain (who signs).
- Provide canonical SKU mapping and sample of 10k SKUs for testing tokenizer fixes.
- Confirm which plant requires EU data residency.

Risks & red flags (notes to self):
- Procurement lead has been slow responding — AE flagged low engagement in last 2 outreach attempts.
- SKU normalization regression could become a pressure point if not quickly remediated; prioritize patch or temporary rule-based fallback.

Draft email to send after meeting (short):
- Subject: Thanks + QBR follow-ups (Atlas Manufacturing)
- Body bullets: restate asks (PO timeline, SKU list, schedule tech kickoff), attach deck, link to next steps doc + action owners.

Slide deck filename suggestion: "Atlas-QBR-2026-Q1-Exec-v1.pptx" (keep short).

Notes for presenter rehearsal:
- Keep exec narrative tight: 10–12 minutes. Save technical nuance for the 15m deep-dive.
- Use customer quotes (Plant 2 supervisor: "we cut exception triage time in half") — verify permission to quote.
- If asked about model drift: be ready to show the evaluation cadence and rollback path.

Version history / provenance (quick):
- v0.1 2026-02-20 Sofia initial skeleton
- v0.2 2026-02-28 added cost model numbers (Liam)
- v0.3 2026-03-10 added regression root cause and proposed fixes (Priya)

Other links / refs:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/ATLAS+Quarterly+Review
- Jira: JIRA-CS-482 (renewal), JIRA-ENG-3192 (SKU normalization bug), JIRA-SRE-77 (regional failover)
- Slack thread: slack://channel/C045ATLAS (customer thread), slack://thread/C04SRE/pxx

TODO (prioritized):
- [ ] Finalize financial appendix and attach spreadsheet (owner: Liam)
- [ ] Confirm quote permission from Plant 2 supervisor (owner: Sofia)
- [ ] Request SKU dataset from Atlas (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Draft procurement PO template to speed approval (owner: AE)

Notes to self: keep the deck <12 slides, make the executive ask explicit, and don't bury the renewal ask under ops details. Be ready to pivot to a technical workshop if the meeting becomes more technical.

End of draft.
